subject: Deployment mode decision & PoC playbook for NovaHealth
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@novahealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode decision & PoC playbook for NovaHealth

Hi Emily / Raj —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, we put together a one-page PoC playbook and a short decision checklist to help pick the right deployment mode (hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem). I attached the PoC playbook (NovaHealth_PoC_Playbook_v1.pdf).

Quick recap of our understanding and open questions so we can lock the PoC scope: 

- Constraints we heard: data residency & compliance (PHI), expected production load ~8–12 QPS at peak, SLO target ~150ms p95 on inference.
- Likely preference: Private VPC since teams handle PHI, but you indicated you wanted to see cost/ops tradeoffs for Dedicated first.

Proposed PoC (high level):
- Duration: 3 weeks (baseline perf + one run of synthetic traffic + one run with sampled production dataset)
- Success criteria (proposed): 1) p95 latency <= 200ms under 10 QPS; 2) end-to-end data handling passes your security checklist (no customer data persists after session); 3) integration: app calls Redwood SDK with <150ms median token latency.
- Stakeholders: Security (TBD), Platform/CloudOps (Raj), Product/ML (Emily), Redwood SE (Ben), Redwood AM (Irene).

As next steps: can you confirm 1) whether Security requires an on-prem package or Private VPC is sufficient, 2) whether you can provide a sanitized sample dataset (or let us run a privacy-safe harness), and 3) target week for kickoff?

I'll schedule a 30-min technical sync next week if you confirm availability — Ben will join to go over infra sizing and the Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@novahealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@novahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Jun 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode decision & PoC playbook for NovaHealth

Thanks, Irene — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Security/compliance: NovaHealth handles PHI; SOC 2 is a minimum. Private VPC would be our default preference because it gives our InfoSec team more comfort around network controls, but we are open to Dedicated if you can show cryptographic separation and attestations. I attached our high-level security requirements (NovaHealth_security_requirements.pdf).
- Performance: our internal estimate is 10 QPS average with occasional spikes to ~18 QPS for short bursts. 150ms p95 is aggressive but desirable — we can review 200ms as the PoC gating number as long as you can show a plan to optimize toward 150ms.
- Dataset: we can provide a synthetically generated dataset that mirrors the token distribution and typical prompts; we will need Redwood to run it in an environment that does not retain raw inputs.

Stakeholders for kickoff:
- Security: Laura Kim (will join the security review call)
- Platform/CloudOps: Raj Patel (cc'd)
- ML/Product: Emily Carter (me)

Target: the week of June 23 or the week after looks feasible for an initial kickoff. Please send the SE/infra runbook and any prerequisites for the Private VPC so I can loop our security team.

Best,
Emily
Emily Carter
Director of Product, NovaHealth

Attachment: NovaHealth_security_requirements.pdf (PDF, 38KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@novahealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@novahealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Jun 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode decision & PoC playbook for NovaHealth

Emily / Raj —

Appreciate the details, this helps. Quick technical notes and a proposed PoC timeline (see attached infra_sizing_novahealth.xlsx and redwood-dedicated-term-sheet.pdf):

- Private VPC: we can provision a Private control plane with customer-managed networking. For PHI workloads that cannot leave your VPC, we recommend our Private deployment (VPC peering + customer-managed NAT). PoC prerequisites: a small test VPC with a reachable bastion host and an S3-compatible endpoint for artifacts.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool is an alternative if you want Redwood-managed networking but with strong tenant isolation. This gives faster time-to-onboard but requires us to provide attestations for crypto and data handling.

Proposed PoC plan (detailed):
Week 0 (prep, 3 business days): architecture signoff, security checklist, test data delivery, access accounts
Week 1: baseline performance (hosted vs dedicated microbench) + make quick kernel/quantization recommendations
Week 2: run synthetic + sampled data experiments at expected QPS; iterate on batching/kv cache settings
Week 3: final run, joint review, handoff docs and recommended next-step deployment and costs

Success criteria (we recommend):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms under steady 10 QPS, with plan to get to 150ms via caching & optimized kernels
- Throughput: sustain a 20 QPS 30s spike without >1% error rate
- Security: pass NovaHealth checklist (no persisted raw inputs, audit logs enabled, KMS for keys)
- Integration: app can call the Redwood SDK with retry/fallback to lower-cost model variant
\Open items for NovaHealth to confirm:
1) Can Security accept Private VPC (our preferred for PHI) vs insisting on full on-prem?
2) Will you provide the sanitized sample dataset by the week of Jun 16?
3) Who will be our primary contact in Security (full name + email) so we can send a dedicated security onboarding pack?
I'll follow up with a short runbook and the infra sizing sheet so Ops can validate port/routing requirements.
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Security will likely accept Private VPC if Redwood can provide the formal onboarding pack and the network diagram (please include all egress endpoints and KMS key flow). Laura Kim from Security will need a 60-min review; I'll introduce her after we have the runbook.
- We can provide a synthetic dataset by Jun 16. I will confirm ownership for that (likely Jake from CloudOps will deliver the sample).
- Confirming stakeholders: Security (Laura Kim), Platform/CloudOps (Raj Patel + Jake Morrison), Product (Emily Carter), ML (internal lead TBD).

Proposed kickoff: Jun 23rd — 30 min technical kickoff to align runbook and get accounts/VPC test access in motion. Can Redwood propose two 30-min slots that week?

Action items:
- Redwood (Irene/Ben): send runbook + network diagram + security onboarding pack (Ben said he would)
- NovaHealth (Raj): confirm dataset owner and target delivery (aiming for Jun 16)

Thanks,
Raj
